title: Entry point: the course home and linear curriculum
description: Start here: index.php is the landing page (hero + one interactive tile per course part) and index_full.php renders the entire curriculum in reading order by including every lesson module in sequence. Reading these two files together shows how a reader discovers and navigates the whole book, and where every lesson plugs in.
languageLesson: No build step: index_full.php is a single PHP template that pulls lessons in via functions.php's incl("Human Title", "slug") helper — the linear course order is declared by hand, one line per lesson.

title: The course shell: server-side infrastructure (functions.php)
description: functions.php is the backbone every page depends on. It parses each lesson's <!-- COURSE_METADATA --> block to auto-build the drawer/index/progress, provides the js/css/incl asset loaders, the post-load JS orchestrator, and renders all the chrome (theme/topics/reader toggles, drawer, module nav, hero constellation). This is the single most important file for understanding how the shell is assembled.
languageLesson: The drawer is generated by scanning lesson files: parse_course_metadata() reads each file's metadata comment, and render_module_nav()/get_module_nav_data() emit the prev/next data that start.js later wires up.

title: Client runtime: markdown, citations, and bootstrapping
description: helper.js renders each lesson's Markdown (protecting LaTeX and the index), processes \cite/\footcite macros against the bibliography, handles typography and lazy section init, and runs the global dark-mode observer. start.js is the site-wide bootstrap: Temml LaTeX rendering with a right-click source popup, dark mode, the mobile drawer, prev/next nav, the auto-glossary, and the loader checklist. Together they turn static .php prose into a living page.
languageLesson: Lesson JS registers a loader in window.__moduleLoaderQueue; loader.js runs each loader concurrently (yielding once so the browser can paint) and ticks off a visible checklist — a dependency-free module system with no bundler.

title: Design system and reading comfort
description: style.css is the single global stylesheet: the --mn-* design tokens (cream-paper light palette with a full dark-mode override), self-hosted fonts, and every component style from the course shell down to Tufte sidenotes, aurora clusters, and the ~1,000 dark-mode rescue rules. polish.js and typography_fix.js layer on the reading comfort — anchors, scroll-spy, copy buttons, citation previews, and silent typographic autocorrect.
languageLesson: Theming is pure CSS custom properties: start.js toggles html.dark and a MutationObserver in helper.js re-renders charts — no per-theme JS, just a token swap plus a watcher.

title: Personalization, progress, and search
description: topics.js is the personalization engine (window.BlogTopics): a topic picker, a math-comfort slider, audience presets, and per-lesson 'learned' tracking that tuck/dim/reveal in-lesson sections and home tiles. progress_tracker.js paints the segmented 'where I've been' bar, and the search trio (search.php endpoint, search_lib.php indexer, search.js overlay) gives Ctrl/Cmd+K full-text search with normal/regex/fuzzy modes.
languageLesson: Persistence is dual: state lives in localStorage and is mirrored to a size-guarded cookie (topics_pref) so it survives the static-file deployment; the cookie write is skipped once near 4 KB.

title: Part 1 — Foundations: the bedrock lessons
description: The book opens with history and math. history.php + history.js trace the convergence of counting tools, number systems, logic, and computation into AI (with an OR/XOR separability demo), and language.php + language.php's timeline run language from Sanskrit to LLMs. Then the four math chapters lay the groundwork: numerical foundations (math_i), linear algebra (math_ii), high-dimensional geometry and type theory (math_iii + math_iii_hott.js), and affine maps & the ReLU fold (math_iv + math_iv_affine.js).
languageLesson: Lessons interleave inline JS: math_iv_affine.js keeps a DOM-free pure-math core (matrices, folds, Hopf tubes) separate from its five canvas labs, and guards the shared math pipeline with an IntersectionObserver-based lazy init.

title: Part 1 — The geometry and statistics trilogy
description: Foundations finish with three deep 'working mathematics' chapters that tie each mathematical object to the layer that uses it. geometry_i.php is a history of geometry (shells to Riemannian manifolds); geometry_ii.php is the geometric toolkit behind networks (inner product, SVD, convolution, symmetry); geometry_iii.php is working algebraic topology (homology, homotopy, persistent homology). statistics_i/ii.php + statistics.js add probability, inference, entropy, and the LLM probability labs.
languageLesson: statistics.js is a single shared lab re-bootstrapped by thin loaders (statistics_i.js / statistics_ii.js guarded by window.__statisticsModuleLoaded), so the same ~20 Plotly labs run standalone or inside the combined course page.

title: Part 2 — How Neural Networks Learn
description: The learning mechanics, in reading order: the smallest network (minimalneuron), why non-linearity is needed (activationlab), what loss is (losslab), the derivative as a steepness check (derivativelab), and differentiation (differentiation). This is the conceptual spine that makes backprop and automatic differentiation land.
languageLesson: Every lab is a self-contained module exposing one global namespace (e.g. a 'LossLab' object) plus a load…Module() entry point; TF.js is used for the live-training demos, Plotly for the static plots.

title: Part 2 — Backprop, autodiff, optimization & live training
description: The payoff of Part 2: backproplab.js animates a forward/backward pass through a 3-4-4-2 net with hoverable cones of influence; autodiff.js builds a tape-based reverse-mode engine and a gradient-landscape animator; optimizerlab.js races SGD/Momentum/Adam; and traininglab.js/trainiglab.php train a live XOR network with decision boundaries and weight heatmaps. reinforcement_learning.php closes with the math of RL and RLHF/DPO.
languageLesson: backproplab.js renders the network as SVG with animated forward/backward pulses and derives per-neuron equations with LaTeX underbraces on click — the same 'make the math touchable' philosophy as the rest of the book.

title: Part 3 — Deep Learning & Vision
description: Deep-learning mechanics first: deeplearninglab (single neuron to deep nets, UAP, residual connections), resnetlab (vanishing gradients vs the residual superhighway), overandunderfittinglab (bias-variance and the extrapolation/hallucination metaphor), normalizationlab (Layer/Group Norm), and topology (homeomorphisms bound a network's power). Then the vision stack: computer_vision.js runs live TF.js convolutions over a stop sign, with deconvolution, inceptionism, and origami's ReLU-folding picture.
languageLesson: computer_vision.js runs real convolutions through TF.js and computes the per-pixel convolution math on hover, while origami.js folds the data manifold in 1-D/3-D to show how ReLU stacks manufacture linear separability.

title: Part 4 — The Transformer Revolution
description: The flagship part. The from-scratch trainable transformer (transformer.php + transformer.js) assembles tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, attention, FFN, unembedding, loss, and optimizer into one machine — instrumented by provenance.js (hover any number to see its computation), tda_live.js (live topological TDA), and transformer_layer_summary.js (what each layer is doing). The supporting lessons walk the pieces: tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, attention, diffusion, algorithms, and mechanistic interpretability.
languageLesson: transformer.js implements a full decoder-only Transformer in the browser (causal multi-head attention, pre-LN, GELU, sinusoidal PE) and trains it with TensorFlow.js; provenance.js hooks onForward to build a value-matched registry so every rendered number is hoverable.

title: Part 5 — Making AI Useful
description: Practical LLM application: promptengineering, finetuninglab (SFT → DPO/GRPO → RLHF), reasoning & test-time compute, contextwindows ('lost in the middle'), the retrieval stack (rag, vectorsearch, websearch), agents, and the reliability/serving concerns (hallucinations, reliability, inference_optimization, production_serving). These are the chapters that turn a trained model into a product.
languageLesson: The retrieval lessons (rag.js, vectorsearch.js, websearch.js) each ship an interactive pipeline diagram plus a tiny in-browser search that scores documents with a BM25-like keyword score and tag-based cosine similarity — the same search machinery used by the site's own search_lib.php.

title: Part 6 — Bigger Questions & the closing arc
description: The book closes on the ecosystem and frontier: the global AI ecosystem, the untold history, the mind that built machines, the wider world of models beyond LLMs, deep theory, frontier topics, alignment, law, philosophy, unexpected capabilities, AI-for-science, existential risk, myths, software, and the interactive appendix. These set the technical content in its historical, social, and ethical frame.

title: Supporting subsystems: demos, Python references, Coq, and QA
description: Finally, the machinery behind the book. lndw/ is a standalone 'Wie funktionieren LLMs?' presentation deck (presentation.js engine + intuition/embedding/attention slides + sheaves/HoTT decks) that previews the same interactive visualizations. py/ mirrors the in-browser lessons in runnable Python (autodiff, minimal-neuron XOR, vision classifiers). coq/coherent_world_models/ is the 19-file Coq formalization of the 'Coherent World Models' chapter. And the tests/ + darkmode-ci/ suites are what keep it all correct: PHP/JS/link/typo/LaTeX validators, headless layout guards, and the Puppeteer dark-mode screenshot CI.
languageLesson: The QA layer is a no-framework test battery: php_validator.py strips PHP/comments then stack-checks HTML tags; js_validator.py is a hand-rolled tokenizer + regex lint; and darkmode-ci's test.js scrolls each page, toggles html.dark, screenshots, and lets autofix.js write safe CSS back into style.css.
